title: Standards watchdog resumes Farage probe as rivals slam needless byelection

paragraphs.en: Nigel Farage’s attempt to draw the sting from inquiries into his financial affairs appeared to have backfired on Friday as the standards watchdog reopened its investigation and MPs from all sides condemned the needless byelection.

The Reform UK leader declared victory in the Clacton vote as he was returned with an increased majority and gained more votes than in 2024, saying he had “stuck two fingers up at the entire political establishment”.
However, parliament’s standards commissioner immediately reopened an investigation into whether he should have declared a series of gifts provided to him shortly before the last general election.
These include a £5m personal gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne , first revealed by the Guardian, and further financial support from his friend and convicted fraudster George Cottrell.

Rival parties said the reopening of the inquiry showed Farage’s attempt to avoid scrutiny had failed, with the Labour party chair, Bridget Phillipson, saying he now had “no hiding place” as he tries to “dodge and deflect” criticism.
But at an event to celebrate his win, the Reform UK leader attempted to diminish the significance of the allegations under investigation.

He told GB News: “If I’ve made one sin, it’s that I haven’t filled in a piece of paper. I’ve broken no law, I’ve broken no tax law, I’ve taken no public money … maybe I haven’t filled in a piece of paper. I’m confident I’m right, let’s see where we go.”
The scandal just keeps piling up. And now he’s through that byelection, there’s no hiding place
